title: Make your UI adaptive with Android Studio's AI agent

segments.text: [MUSIC PLAYING]
DON TURNER: Hey, everyone.
I'm Don, and this is Jose.
Today we're going to talk to you about building
adaptive UIs, specifically for mobile and large-screen form
factors.
So generally, when you think about building an adaptive UI,
you think about how it looks on different form factors.
You start with phones, which is still
definitely the most important form factor,
but then you consider tablets, foldables, laptops, desktops,
TV, cars, and a whole bunch of other form factors.
Form factors represent an abstraction for a device's size
and capabilities, and they give us
a shared vocabulary that makes it
easy to discuss how our apps should look
on a given class of devices.
After all, we all know what a tablet is, right?
OK, so let's test that.
Hands up if you think this is a tablet.

Do you think this is a tablet?

OK.

plugged into that monitor.

So my point here is that we don't all
agree on what form factors are.
Devices can have multiple form factors.
They can switch between them instantly,
and they sometimes don't neatly fall into a form factor
category.
And this means that form factors aren't quite as useful as we
once thought they were for designing UIs. Also,
creating form factor-specific UIs can lead to branches
or entire code bases with lots of repeated code and loads
of maintenance requirements.
So a better approach is to design and develop
for UI capabilities such as window size and pointer type.
And this allows you to create an optimal UI,
regardless of the form factor.
And with the APIs and tools that we're going to show you today,
it doesn't have to be a costly investment.
And you never know.
It might actually be fun.

and install skills.

You can download it from GitHub or using Android CLI.

Can you just ask the agent, make my app adaptive?
